evals.name: standard-canadian-receipt-batch
evals.prompt: I have 12 Canadian receipt images in /Users/jacky/.agents/skills/invoice-canada-cpa/references/invoices/canada/. Process them with multi-modal extraction (MiniMax JSON + MinerU markdown), cross-validate using LLM (vendor/date from MiniMax, amounts from MinerU with tie-out check), assign GIFI codes, and write a 3-sheet Excel to round2_cross_validated.xlsx. Validate all 8 quality gates.
evals.expected_output: Excel file with Decisions / Raw_Outputs / Validation_Report sheets. 12 rows. All 8 quality gates pass. Source attribution tagged for every field. Tie-out verified (sub+tax=total) for every row. Every GIFI code exists in the CRA list and is neither a generic block header nor a total item.

evals.name: restaurant-discount-receipt
evals.prompt: Process this BBQ restaurant receipt: bbq_95.68_11.02.jpg. The receipt has SubTotal $94.07, 10% DISCOUNT -$9.41, H.S.T. $11.02, TOTAL $95.68. Use the printed SubTotal (not the calculated tax base $84.66). Apply the discounted tie-out formula.
evals.expected_output: subtotal=94.07, discount=9.41, tax=11.02, total=95.68. Tie-out: (94.07 - 9.41) + 11.02 = 95.68 ✓. GIFI code 8523 Meals and entertainment (NOT 8521, which is Advertising; NOT 8520, which is the generic block header). tax_treatment notes the 50% ITA 67.1 limit as a separate axis. Source attribution for each field.

evals.name: zero-tax-grocery-receipt
evals.prompt: Process this T&T Supermarket basic-grocery receipt: tnt_64.78_0.jpg. The receipt has SubTotal $64.78, HST $0.00 (zero-rated basic groceries), TOTAL $64.78. Use is None checks (not 'or -1') to avoid false tie-out failures on zero-tax receipts.
evals.expected_output: subtotal=64.78, tax=0.0, total=64.78. Tie-out passes (64.78 + 0.0 = 64.78). GIFI code 8523 Meals and entertainment if staff food, or 9130 Supplies if operational — either is acceptable when justified by stated use. Must NOT be 8521. Note: tax=0.0 is valid, not missing.

evals.name: sideways-rotated-receipt
evals.prompt: Process this sideways-photographed Costco tire receipt: costco_971.75_111.79.jpg. Don't rotate the image. MinerU may partially extract the values. If vendor/date fail in both MiniMax and MinerU, mark them as VISUAL. The receipt has 4 tires at $209.99, $20 levy, HST $111.79, total $971.75.
evals.expected_output: subtotal=859.96, tax=111.79, total=971.75. Vendor may be marked VISUAL. GIFI code 9281 Vehicle expenses (CRA lists tires explicitly under 9281). NOT 8520. Treated as current expense; review_required=true flagged due to amount.

evals.name: chinese-english-mixed-receipt
evals.prompt: Process this Chinese-English mixed BBQ receipt: bbq_95.68_11.02.jpg. Vendor is '有局儿烧烤' in Chinese. Use MiniMax to extract the English transliteration. Preserve the Chinese in a vendor_cn field. Skip Tesseract (it will garble Chinese).

evals.name: filename-mismatch-detection
evals.prompt: There's a file costco_1315.46_144.62.jpg (the filename was renamed from costco_315.46_144.62.jpg because it was missing the leading '1'). Verify the rename happened, check that the filename numbers now match the receipt contents, and confirm all 8 quality gates pass.
evals.expected_output: Filename check: 1315.46 matches receipt total, 144.62 matches receipt tax. Mismatch resolved. All gates pass.

evals.name: tire-purchase-expense-vs-capital
evals.prompt: Process the Costco tire receipt costco_971.75_111.79.jpg. The 4 tires at $209.99 + $20 levy + $111.79 HST = $971.75. The single transaction exceeds $500. Should this be a current expense or capitalized under CCA Class 10?
evals.expected_output: GIFI code 9281 Vehicle expenses. Treated as a CURRENT EXPENSE, not capital — CRA explicitly lists 'tires' among the contents of 9281. Capitalization under CCA Class 10 applies to acquiring the vehicle itself, not to replacement tires. Amount is large, so review_required=true and the note should say 'Large vehicle-expense amount; CPA to confirm expense vs capital treatment.' deductible_pct='100%'. The skill must NOT assert a hard '>$500 = capital' rule.

evals.name: 50-percent-meals-deduction-rule
evals.prompt: Process the BBQ restaurant receipt bbq_95.68_11.02.jpg. Per ITA 67.1, only 50% of meal expenses are deductible. Apply the rule at classification time — do not halve the recorded expense (the 50% is applied at filing time by the CPA). Set the deductible_pct to '50%' in the workpaper.
evals.expected_output: GIFI 8523 Meals and entertainment, deductible_pct='50% (ITA 67.1)', schedule_1_flag=true. The recorded expense in the workpaper stays at $95.68 (full amount). GIFI mapping and tax treatment are recorded in separate columns — the 50% limit must not alter the GIFI code or the recorded amount.

evals.name: generic-parent-trap
evals.prompt: For the 12-receipt batch, produce the GIFI summary. For each code assigned, state its parent code and whether it is a generic block header. Then confirm: is 8520 equal to the sum of 8521 + 8522 + 8523 + 8524?
evals.expected_output: No row uses a generic block header (8520, 8620, 8710, 8760, 8860, 8910, 8960, 9060, 9130, 9150, 9220) when a specific child code applies. gifi_parent and is_generic are populated for every row. The answer to the summing question is NO — CRA states a generic item does not represent the total of the items in its block, so 8520 must never be computed as the sum of 8521-8524.

evals.name: gifi-code-validity-gate
evals.prompt: Run quality gate 5 (GIFI validity) over the workpaper. For each assigned GIFI code, verify it exists in the CRA GIFI list, is not a generic block header, and is not a total item.
evals.expected_output: Gate reports pass/fail per row. Codes that do not exist in CRA Appendix A (e.g. 8575, 8530, 8540, 8545, 8550, 8560, 8565, 8605) are rejected.
